summary.title: Brew & Coffee Co. Ordering Web Application - Revised STRIDE Model
summary.description: Academic threat model of four workflows: customer ordering and payment confirmation, barista order-status updates, manager sales reports, and administrator menu creation. Components, data flows, and threats are conceptual; controls are proposed and are not assertions that the production system implements them. Severity estimates use qualitative impact and likelihood assumptions and should be validated by the system owner.

diagrams.title: Customer Places an Order
diagrams.placeholder: Customer submits an order; server validates details, coordinates tokenized payment, stores order/payment state, and returns confirmation.

data.name: Customer
data.description: External user or third-party service interacting with this workflow.

data.name:
Browser Client
(Frontend)
data.description: Client-side user interface. Treat all browser input and storage as untrusted.

threats.title: Customer session theft
threats.description: An attacker using a stolen session cookie could impersonate a customer and place orders or read order history.
threats.mitigation: Use Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookies, short sessions, session rotation after login, and revocation on logout.

data.name:
Web
Application
Server
data.description: Server-side application logic, authenticated APIs, authorization and database/payment integrations.

threats.title: Order API customer impersonation
threats.description: The order API might accept a forged or stolen identity token without independently validating it.
threats.mitigation: Validate token issuer, audience, signature and expiry server-side; bind every order request to its authenticated user.

threats.title: Client-controlled order pricing
threats.description: The server might trust a price or discount sent by the browser, causing incorrect totals and fraudulent discounts.
threats.mitigation: Use canonical menu prices and discount rules on the server; calculate totals independently of client-provided values.

threats.title: Disputed order submission
threats.description: A customer could deny placing an order if order creation events cannot be linked reliably to an authenticated account.
threats.mitigation: Create tamper-resistant order audit events with user ID, timestamp, order ID and request correlation ID.

threats.title: Unauthorized order-history access
threats.description: An API may return another customer's delivery details and purchases if order IDs lack ownership checks.
threats.mitigation: Enforce object-level authorization on every order/history request and minimize returned personal data.

threats.title: Order endpoint request flood
threats.description: Repeated order requests or expensive validation could exhaust server capacity and disrupt checkout.
threats.mitigation: Apply per-user/IP rate limits, request quotas, resource timeouts, monitoring and service-level throttling.

data.name: Payment Gateway
data.description: External user or third-party service interacting with this workflow.

data.name: MongoDB Database
data.description: MongoDB persistence used by this workflow. Collection design and deployment configuration are not verified.

threats.title: Direct modification of stored order state
threats.description: Compromised database credentials could alter item prices, payment flags, or order status outside normal business logic.
threats.mitigation: Use least-privilege database accounts, protected access, audited writes and restricted administrative credentials.

threats.title: MongoDB customer data exposure
threats.description: Misconfiguration or compromised database credentials could expose order history, names, and delivery information.
threats.mitigation: Restrict network access and database roles; encrypt traffic and backups; avoid storing unnecessary personal data.

data.name: Send Order Request
data.description: Browser submits basket and customer order data to order API

threats.title: Order request parameter manipulation
threats.description: An attacker can change quantities, product IDs, or discount parameters in an intercepted or crafted API request.
threats.mitigation: Enforce HTTPS, validate all request fields, allowlist purchasable product IDs and verify all pricing server-side.

threats.title: Order confirmation leakage
threats.description: Order details could reach a shared cache or a browser session belonging to a different customer.
threats.mitigation: Return only the authenticated customer's data and use no-store cache directives for personalized responses.

data.name: Tokenized Payment Request
data.description: Backend sends gateway a request using tokenized payment reference

threats.title: Payment-token leakage
threats.description: Payment references or access tokens could be exposed if gateway calls are logged or sent through insecure channels.
threats.mitigation: Use TLS to the gateway, keep gateway secrets server-side, redact sensitive tokens from logs and rotate keys.

data.name: Transaction Response
data.description: Payment provider conveys transaction outcome to backend

threats.title: Forged payment-success response
threats.description: An attacker could fabricate a payment success callback and cause the system to release an unpaid order.
threats.mitigation: Verify gateway signatures or authenticate provider callbacks and confirm transaction state server-to-server.

threats.title: Payment response replay
threats.description: Replayed or modified gateway responses could trigger duplicate captures or incorrect state transitions.
threats.mitigation: Validate transaction IDs and amounts, enforce idempotency, reject replayed event IDs and track payment state transitions.

data.name:
Record Order &
Payment Status
data.description: Backend persists order and verified payment state

threats.title: Forged paid status persisted
threats.description: An application or database integration flaw could store paid=true before the provider confirms successful payment.
threats.mitigation: Persist payment status only after verified provider confirmation; use atomic updates and a constrained state machine.

threats.title: Excess information in database response
threats.description: A broad query may return customer PII that the checkout handler does not need.
threats.mitigation: Apply field-level projections and least-privilege read scopes; avoid transmitting or logging unused personal fields.

diagrams.title: Barista Updates Order Status
diagrams.placeholder: Barista authenticates, fetches pending orders, and requests authorized status transitions.

data.name: Barista
data.description: External user or third-party service interacting with this workflow.

data.name:
Frontend
(Staff Interface)
data.description: Client-side user interface. Treat all browser input and storage as untrusted.

threats.title: Stolen barista session
threats.description: An attacker who steals a barista session could view incoming orders and perform staff functions.
threats.mitigation: Use short-lived secure sessions, token rotation, staff MFA where feasible, and logout/invalidation on role changes.

data.name:
Web
Application
Server
data.description: Server-side application logic, authenticated APIs, authorization and database/payment integrations.

threats.title: Unauthorized order-status transitions
threats.description: A malicious request could change an order directly from Pending to Completed without permitted workflow checks.
threats.mitigation: Enforce allowed state transitions, validate order existence and check every update against staff permissions.

threats.title: Barista bypasses role-based access
threats.description: A barista could call manager or administrator API routes if authorization is enforced only in the frontend.
threats.mitigation: Enforce server-side RBAC on each protected endpoint and deny access by default.

threats.title: Untraceable order-status change
threats.description: A staff member could deny updating a customer order if changes lack reliable, tamper-resistant audit records.
threats.mitigation: Record staff ID, order ID, before/after status, time and request ID in protected audit logs.

threats.title: Excessive incoming-order polling
threats.description: Automated polling of the pending-order endpoint could overload the server and interrupt barista operations.
threats.mitigation: Rate-limit polling, cache/restrict query frequency and use bounded pagination or event-driven updates.

data.name: MongoDB Database
data.description: MongoDB persistence used by this workflow. Collection design and deployment configuration are not verified.

threats.title: Database write bypass of status rules
threats.description: An attacker with excessive database permissions could update orders without server state-transition checks.
threats.mitigation: Limit database write privileges, isolate application credentials and audit privileged modifications.

data.name:
Authenticate &
Authorize
data.description: Logical identity verification and access-control service. Deployment location is unspecified.

threats.title: Staff credential stuffing
threats.description: Reused staff credentials could be tested against the authentication process to obtain a valid session.
threats.mitigation: Use credential-stuffing detection, MFA, login throttling and monitoring of anomalous attempts.

threats.title: Stale staff privileges accepted
threats.description: A deactivated or demoted staff member might retain authorization if old claims or sessions remain valid.
threats.mitigation: Validate role claims server-side, expire/rotate sessions promptly and revoke access when staff roles change.

data.name: Order List
data.description: Server sends incoming order list to authenticated barista frontend.

threats.title: Order list exposed in shared browser
threats.description: The staff order list could persist in browser caches or become visible in a session used by another person.
threats.mitigation: Use no-store headers, short staff sessions and automatic logout for unattended terminals.

threats.title: Unrestricted pending-order listing
threats.description: The order-list API may expose customer names or contact information beyond a barista's job needs.
threats.mitigation: Check barista role and scope on the server, minimize customer fields and paginate order results.

data.name:
Authenticate
Barista
data.description: Backend requests barista authentication and role verification

threats.title: Replayed staff authentication credentials
threats.description: Stolen authentication material could be reused to impersonate a barista during a login request.
threats.mitigation: Require TLS, protect credentials and verify short-lived challenges or tokens in the authentication service.

data.name:
Authorize
Barista
data.description: Authentication service returns result and verified role attributes

threats.title: Forged authorization decision
threats.description: An attacker could try to alter a role or authorization decision returned to the application server.
threats.mitigation: Authenticate the identity provider, protect transport, validate signed tokens and ignore user-supplied roles.

data.name: Update Pending Orders
data.description: Backend updates validated order state in the database

threats.title: Tampered database status update
threats.description: A crafted status-update operation could target an order outside a barista's assigned scope.
threats.mitigation: Bind the update to the authenticated actor, enforce permitted order scope and apply conditional atomic updates.

threats.title: Unbounded pending-order query
threats.description: Missing pagination or indexing could cause expensive queries that degrade availability during busy periods.
threats.mitigation: Set query limits and timeouts, use appropriate indexes and monitor slow queries.

diagrams.title: Manager Accesses Basic Sales Reports
diagrams.placeholder: Manager authenticates and requests a sales report built from MongoDB sales data.

data.name: Manager
data.description: External user or third-party service interacting with this workflow.

data.name:
Client Side
(Frontend)
data.description: Manager-facing browser frontend; an untrusted client, not an external actor.

threats.title: Manager session hijacking
threats.description: A stolen manager session may permit an attacker to access sensitive sales reports.
threats.mitigation: Use secure cookies, short session lifetimes, MFA and fresh authorization checks for privileged reports.

data.name:
Web
Application
Server
data.description: Server-side application logic, authenticated APIs, authorization and database/payment integrations.

threats.title: Sales-report role check bypass
threats.description: A barista or customer could access manager reports through direct API calls if server-side role checks are weak.
threats.mitigation: Enforce server-side RBAC and deny report endpoints unless the current user has the required manager role.

threats.title: Manipulated report query filters
threats.description: Crafted report filters might alter aggregations, expose unauthorized branches, or distort displayed sales totals.
threats.mitigation: Allowlist filters, validate date ranges and branch scope, and use safe parameterized database queries.

threats.title: Unaudited report access
threats.description: A staff member could deny accessing or exporting sensitive sales information if request logs lack attribution.
threats.mitigation: Audit report access by staff ID, dataset/filters, timestamp, outcome and correlation ID.

threats.title: Heavy report aggregation requests
threats.description: Repeated large-range report requests could exhaust CPU or database resources and impact checkout.
threats.mitigation: Restrict allowed date ranges, rate-limit report endpoints and cache approved aggregate reports.

threats.title: Report includes unauthorized customer fields
threats.description: A report may accidentally include transaction-level personal information when only aggregate metrics are required.
threats.mitigation: Return minimum necessary aggregates, mask identifying fields and enforce response-level data minimization.

data.name: MongoDB Database
data.description: MongoDB persistence used by this workflow. Collection design and deployment configuration are not verified.

threats.title: Sales records altered at source
threats.description: Unauthorized database writes could falsify revenue totals, refunds or performance summaries.
threats.mitigation: Use role-separated write access, audited changes and reconciliation against immutable transaction records.

threats.title: Broad database read privileges
threats.description: A report service account with unrestricted collection access could disclose personal or operational data.
threats.mitigation: Grant read access only to approved collections/views and minimize database/network exposure.

threats.title: Forged manager access token
threats.description: A caller could present a fabricated or stolen authorization token when requesting a sales report.
threats.mitigation: Validate signature, issuer, audience, expiry and role claims; reject unsigned or expired tokens.

data.name: Request Sales Report
data.description: Manager client supplies report selection to server

threats.title: Cross-branch report access
threats.description: A user could change the requested branch ID to retrieve reports outside their authorized area.
threats.mitigation: Derive scope from server-verified permissions rather than trusting submitted report parameters.

data.name: Formatted Sales Report
data.description: Server returns formatted report to manager client

threats.title: Cached manager report exposed
threats.description: A personalized sales report could be cached and later served to an unauthorized browser session.
threats.mitigation: Use private/no-store cache headers, recheck report permissions and prevent report identifiers from granting access.

threats.title: Unbounded reporting database query
threats.description: Unindexed grouping or unrestricted lookback periods can overload the MongoDB reporting collection.
threats.mitigation: Use indexes, bounded aggregation pipelines, query timeouts and restrictive report date ranges.

data.name: Unformatted Sales Data
data.description: Database returns raw/aggregatable data to report service

threats.title: Raw sales records overexposed
threats.description: Database query results may contain customer or payment-related fields not needed for report aggregation.
threats.mitigation: Use aggregate projections and TLS on internal links; avoid returning unnecessary transaction fields.

diagrams.title: Administrator Adds New Menu Item
diagrams.placeholder: Administrator authenticates and submits validated details for creation of a new menu item.

data.name: Administrator
data.description: External user or third-party service interacting with this workflow.

data.name: Client Side
data.description: Client-side user interface. Treat all browser input and storage as untrusted.

threats.title: Administrator session theft
threats.description: An attacker with an administrator session could create fake menu items or manipulate displayed prices.
threats.mitigation: Use strong authentication, MFA, secure short-lived cookies and session revalidation for administrative actions.

data.name: Menu Item Information
data.description: Admin client submits new product attributes

threats.title: Modified menu creation payload
threats.description: An attacker could change menu prices, category, or product status before a create request reaches the server.
threats.mitigation: Use TLS, schema validation and allowlisted server-side fields; never rely solely on frontend validation.

data.name: Login Request
data.description: Admin client requests authentication from backend

threats.title: Administrator credentials exposed in transit
threats.description: Credentials may be intercepted if login requests are transmitted without authenticated encryption.
threats.mitigation: Require HTTPS/TLS, disable insecure redirects, never place credentials in URLs and avoid logging secrets.

data.name: Session Token
data.description: Backend returns session credential after successful login

threats.title: Reused or forged administrative token
threats.description: A stolen or incorrectly validated token may let an attacker impersonate an administrator.
threats.mitigation: Sign and validate tokens, use short expiries, bind privileges to server-side role checks and support revocation.

data.name: Menu Item Details
data.description: Validated menu item attributes are stored in database

threats.title: Menu item write payload tampering
threats.description: Improperly constrained database inserts could persist unintended attributes or malformed menu records.
threats.mitigation: Enforce database schema constraints and least-privilege writes; use validated application-generated inserts.

threats.title: Forged database create acknowledgement
threats.description: An integration error could treat an unverified response as proof a menu item was actually persisted.
threats.mitigation: Inspect acknowledged write results and item IDs, handle failures explicitly and verify state before confirmation.

threats.title: Auth response privilege modification
threats.description: A forged authentication response could claim an administrator role that the provider never granted.
threats.mitigation: Validate signed authentication assertions and map roles from trusted server-side records, not client content.

data.name:
Web
Application
Server
data.description: Server-side application logic, authenticated APIs, authorization and database/payment integrations.

threats.title: Non-admin creates menu item
threats.description: A customer or lower-privilege staff member may invoke the item-creation endpoint if role checks are missing.
threats.mitigation: Enforce server-side administrator authorization for every menu mutation and deny by default.

threats.title: Unauthorized menu-price setting
threats.description: A crafted item-creation request could set negative prices, unexpected fields or a hidden publication state.
threats.mitigation: Validate item schema and numeric ranges, allowlist editable fields and use controlled workflow approval where needed.

threats.title: Menu creation cannot be attributed
threats.description: An administrator could deny creating a menu item if the application does not keep trustworthy change history.
threats.mitigation: Audit actor ID, item ID, original values, timestamp and request outcome; restrict audit-log changes.

threats.title: Duplicate menu item creation flood
threats.description: Repeated item-creation submissions could fill the database or disrupt legitimate administrative work.
threats.mitigation: Apply request limits, idempotency keys, maximum request size and validation before database writes.

data.name: MongoDB Database
data.description: MongoDB persistence used by this workflow. Collection design and deployment configuration are not verified.

threats.title: Unauthorized menu collection update
threats.description: Excessive database privileges could allow menu data to be edited directly outside the authorized admin API.
threats.mitigation: Use least-privilege database accounts, network isolation, audit logging and protected database administration.

data.name:
Authorization
Provider
data.description: Logical identity verification and access-control service. Deployment location is unspecified.

threats.title: Fake identity-provider token
threats.description: An attacker could present an identity token with a forged administrator claim to the application.
threats.mitigation: Validate provider identity and token signature, issuer, audience, expiry and role assignment.

threats.title: Authentication provider unavailable
threats.description: If the authorization service is overwhelmed or unavailable, staff cannot authenticate to manage the menu.
threats.mitigation: Use availability monitoring, bounded retries, circuit breakers and documented administrative recovery procedures.
